2.label: Intermediate
2.focus: apply vocabulary and grammar in context

3.label: Bac Challenge
3.focus: analyse, infer and produce structured language

standard.label: Terminale
standard.style: clear English at final-year secondary level

ultra_simple.label: Very simple
ultra_simple.style: very accessible English with occasional French support

concepts.title: Hobbies and recreational activities

explanations.standard: The unit explores how hobbies and recreational activities can support well-being, relationships, self-expression, confidence, skills and sometimes income.
explanations.simple: Hobbies can help people relax, learn skills, connect with others and feel better.
explanations.ultra_simple: A hobby is something you enjoy in your free time. It can help your mind, your body or your relationships.

common_mistakes: thinking recreation has only one possible benefit
confusing a hobby with a compulsory task

concepts.title: Listening to a personal testimony

explanations.standard: The listening task asks for specific details from a personal testimony about a young Cameroonian fashion designer in New York.
explanations.simple: Listen for names, places, actions and evidence of success.
explanations.ultra_simple: Read the question first, then listen for that exact detail.

common_mistakes: answering from general knowledge instead of the audio
inventing details that are not heard

concepts.title: Voiced and unvoiced consonants

explanations.standard: Voiced consonants involve vocal-cord vibration; unvoiced consonants do not. The source lists examples of both groups.
explanations.simple: Touch your throat: voiced sounds vibrate; unvoiced sounds do not.
explanations.ultra_simple: Voiced = your throat vibrates. Unvoiced = no vibration.

common_mistakes: classifying by spelling instead of the sound
treating pronunciation practice as a writing exercise

concepts.title: Skimming for the main idea

explanations.standard: To skim, read titles/subheadings, inspect pictures/charts and read the first sentence of each paragraph before detailed reading.
explanations.simple: Do not read every word first. Use the big clues and first sentences to catch the main idea.
explanations.ultra_simple: Skim = read fast for the big idea, not every detail.

common_mistakes: reading every word before finding the topic
confusing skimming with guessing without evidence

concepts.title: Understanding personal stories about hobbies

explanations.standard: The four stories show different benefits: stress management, creative balance, environmental beauty and income, confidence and participation.
explanations.simple: Each person has a different hobby and a different benefit.
explanations.ultra_simple: Ask two questions: What is the hobby? How did it help the person?

common_mistakes: mixing details from different people
remembering the hobby but not its benefit

concepts.title: Vocabulary of recreation and well-being

explanations.standard: The unit builds vocabulary for recreation, emotions, clothing, confidence and care.
explanations.simple: Learn each word with a short meaning and use it in context.
explanations.ultra_simple: Word + meaning + example: that is the fastest way to remember it.

common_mistakes: confusing shy with stressed
confusing self-confidence with balance

concepts.title: Phrasal verbs

explanations.standard: A phrasal verb combines a verb with an adverb or preposition to create an idiomatic meaning.
explanations.simple: The small word changes the meaning of the verb: calm down, turn down, call off.

common_mistakes: translating each word separately
choosing a particle only because it sounds familiar

concepts.title: Prepositional phrases

explanations.standard: Prepositional phrases begin with prepositions and can function adjectivally or adverbially.
explanations.simple: These phrases begin with words like at, in, on or under and add information about time, place, manner or description.
explanations.ultra_simple: Look for the preposition first: at, in, on, under...

common_mistakes: using 'of the world' where the source uses 'in the world'
using 'with time' instead of 'on time'

concepts.title: Formal letter structure

explanations.standard: The source models a formal letter with sender and recipient details, date, salutation, subject, organised body paragraphs and a polite close.
explanations.simple: A formal letter needs clear addresses, a subject, organised paragraphs and a polite ending.
explanations.ultra_simple: Think: who writes, who receives, why you write, what you propose, polite ending.

common_mistakes: writing without a clear subject
putting all ideas in one paragraph
using an informal tone

concepts.title: Arguing for recreational facilities

explanations.standard: The writing task requires a clear case for recreational facilities, linking them to well-being, health, relationships, income and community participation.
explanations.simple: Explain why recreation matters, what the community can do, and how you can help.
explanations.ultra_simple: Problem → benefits → community action → your contribution.

common_mistakes: listing benefits without proposing action
forgetting the learner's own contribution
using an informal tone

adaptive_rules: After two errors on the same concept, suggest Simple English.
After one additional error, suggest Very simple.
After three consecutive correct answers, suggest a higher difficulty.
Exercise difficulty and explanation level remain independent.
